decisions.reason: As a low-cost complementary care product squarely within the firm's established flooring system offer, its option value remains high and there is little evidence yet that it has failed.

This maintenance oil extends the installed base of wooden floors and, despite some assortment complexity from multiple models, it is inexpensive to carry relative to the value of preserving a full care system.
Because it fits the firm's oiled-floor segment and likely has modest carrying costs, management would keep it while market response across variants becomes clearer.
A moisture-protection underlay strengthens the firm's system solution for floor installation, and with no clear negative signal it is worth retaining as an option.

Although this underlay foam is somewhat more replaceable and may overlap with other installation accessories, it is still close to the core offer and cheap enough to keep while demand uncertainty resolves.

The oak parquet line is more resource-intensive and variant-heavy than the accessory products, but it is close to the core flooring business and the growing market makes continued observation more attractive than early withdrawal.
